directAnswer: St. Boniface I was a Roman priest who served as pope from 418 to 422. His election was contested by the archdeacon Eulalius, and the emperor Honorius settled the dispute in Boniface's favor. As pope, he supported St. Augustine against the Pelagians and defended Rome's authority over the churches of eastern Illyricum.

paras: After Zosimus died, a group of clergy chose the archdeacon Eulalius on December 27, 418. The next day, a larger body of priests elected Boniface, an elderly priest. The city prefect sided with Eulalius and reported to Emperor Honorius, who at first recognized him.

Honorius then called a synod to decide the matter and ordered both men to stay away from Rome while it deliberated. When Eulalius returned to the city in defiance of the order before Easter 419, the emperor withdrew his support and recognized Boniface, who took full possession of the see that April. Honorius afterward ordered that disputed elections should be resolved by a new election rather than imperial choice between rivals.

Boniface continued the Roman opposition to Pelagianism. Augustine dedicated to him a treatise answering two Pelagian letters that had been circulating, and Boniface encouraged the African bishops' efforts. The Apiarius dispute with Africa remained unresolved during his reign.

He curbed the special powers that Zosimus had given to the bishop of Arles, restoring the rights of other metropolitans in Gaul. When Emperor Theodosius II tried to place eastern Illyricum under the church of Constantinople, Boniface protested, and Honorius persuaded his nephew to keep the earlier arrangement.
Boniface died on September 4, 422, and was buried at the cemetery of St. Felicitas on the Via Salaria. Little else about him is recorded.

keyFacts: Elected in competition with the archdeacon Eulalius, later considered an antipope
Recognized by Emperor Honorius in April 419
St. Augustine dedicated an anti-Pelagian treatise to him
Buried at the cemetery of St. Felicitas on the Via Salaria

faqs.question: Who was Eulalius?
faqs.answer: Eulalius was a Roman archdeacon elected by a rival faction a day before Boniface. The emperor initially recognized him but later rejected him for defying imperial orders, and he is now counted as an antipope.

faqs.question: How was Pope Boniface I connected to St. Augustine?
faqs.answer: Augustine dedicated his treatise Against Two Letters of the Pelagians to Boniface, who supported the African bishops in opposing Pelagian teaching.
